description:
Prototype branch to measure what handwired-style per-item programs would ask of defk. Context: docs/research/handwired.md. Not a commitment to a GPU backend: docs/scope.md puts GPU with Nx, and a change needs an owner decision and an ADR.

Stages (each ends with numbers or a finding in docs/research/handwired.md; the owner picks whether the next stage runs):
1. CPU baseline. The SEARCH step (the 4.6 to 13.2 ms numbers are for the search, not the highlighter), as literal patterns (error, connection reset) in a shift-and bitmask kernel over 100,000 JSON documents of up to 512 bytes. Compare optimised Elixir (:binary.matches, :re, chunked over all schedulers), defk on one core and over all cores. Reference: handwired lab/json-search/README.md (RegExp 8 to 43 ms one thread, 1.9 to 6.7 ms in 8 workers, GPU 4.5 to 5.2 ms; the author machine, never compared as equals). The script lives in bench/, outside the catalog.
2. f32 cost. Exact FP32 rounding through an [f32] scratch write against f64 defk: exactness and time.
3. Compiler impact inventory. Where the lowering and emitting sections of Defk.Compiler assume C. What a second backend would hook into. Text-level only first.
4. Dialect choice: GPU from C. Check what this Mac supports (Metal, OpenCL, none, via headers and a tiny probe, no heavy run). List what a Linux server would need (OpenMP offload, CUDA or HIP). Hand-write one pure per-item f32 kernel in the dialects that work here and compare it with the existing defk CPU loop as test oracle: agreement, FMA and bit-exactness (defk promises bit-exact results with Elixir mode), launch and transfer cost per call. Pairs with the vector-value study (defk-ulk.5), which covers SIMD and comes first.
5. Optional, owner decides: a throwaway emitter that writes the per-item body once and wraps it per dialect, and a device run.

Rules: Elixir is the default, optimise it first. Read handwired only, never run its code. No sweeping runs, no heavy runs on battery without saying the cost.

comments.text: Stage 1 done on branch defk-snm/handwired-research: bench/handwired_search.exs, result in docs/research/handwired.md (Elixir :binary.matches in 12 chunks 6.8-8.6 ms, defk shift-and 9.2-9.5 ms, quiet machine). Next stage needs the owner's pick.

Stage 1b done: bench/handwired_classes.exs, result in docs/research/handwired.md. defk bit-parallel NFA 14-15 ms in 12 chunks vs :re 19-33 ms; hand-written Elixir anchor+:binary.matches 7-10 ms beats defk; defk wins only without a literal anchor. Quiet machine, one run.

Stage 3 done: compiler impact inventory in docs/research/handwired.md. No IR (lowering returns C text values); about 4,400 of 6,513 compiler lines entangled; GPU cannot keep yield/siglongjmp/normal-scheduler promises as written; recommended attach: small device-kernel frontend (option C), sized by a throwaway spike.

title: Research spike: per-document circuit kernels (handwired) and a GPU target, impact on defk
